data.name: Pro Wrestling Tycoon
data.detailed_description:
Build Your Empire. Book the Cards. Own the Industry.

Pro Wrestling Tycoon is a deep wrestling promotion management sim. Step into a living pro wrestling universe as your own character, grow your promoter skills, and take the reins of a company — from local territory to global recognition.

Every day, the industry moves whether you’re ready or not. Rival promotions book shows, chase talent, and compete for attention. Your job is to keep the lights on, the roster happy, and the fans invested.

Run a Promotion

  • Roster & Contracts - Sign, release, and negotiate with wrestlers and staff. Manage pushes, alignment, brands, and gimmicks.

  • Shows & Booking - Schedule cards, book matches and angles, then run the show.

  • Storytelling - Build feuds, tag teams, stables, and a title picture that keeps fans coming back.

  • Business - Track finances, merchandise, operations, and network deals.

  • Creative & Backstage - Shape your product identity and manage the politics behind the curtain.

  • Injuries & Development - Keep talent healthy, handle fallout, and train the next generation in dojos.

A Living Wrestling World

  • Advance day by day as rival companies compete across the globe

  • Negotiate TV and streaming deals — and keep network relationships strong

  • Follow the industry through news, calendar events, and weekly recaps

  • Browse people, companies, venues, networks, and dojos across the universe

  • React to random world events that shake up the scene

  • Grow your promoter and talent through skills and XP over time

Modding & Steam Workshop Support

There is no single fixed universe — you start from a base mod you create, import, or download.

Author companies, people, networks, venues, dojos, match and wrestler gimmicks, angle beats, injuries, relationships, and random world events. Share mods and picture packs on the Steam Workshop, and build the wrestling world you want to manage.

Key Features

  • Day-by-day wrestling promotion simulation

  • Full card booking with matches, angles, and show presentation

  • Contracts, finances, merchandise, and operations

  • Titles, feuds, tag teams, and stables

  • Networks, venues, dojos, injuries, and developmental systems

  • Deep offline modding tools plus Steam Workshop support

  • Single-player — no always-online requirement for core play

data.short_description: Pro Wrestling Tycoon is a day-by-day wrestling promotion management sim. Book shows, manage contracts and storylines, negotiate network deals, and compete in a living industry of rival companies, news, and backstage drama. Deep modding and Steam Workshop support let you shape the universe.

  • Storage: 500 MB available space

content_descriptors.notes:
Pro Wrestling Tycoon is a text-heavy management simulation of the pro wrestling industry. It does not focus on graphic depictions of sexual acts. Mature themes appear mainly through simulated workplace drama, booking decisions, news, messages, and moddable content.

Violence is central to the setting. Matches, angles, and show presentation can include staged combat, dangerous spots, injuries, rehab, and suspensions. Talent may suffer serious injuries, and characters can die during a save through natural causes, health issues, accidents, in-ring incidents, or overdose. These events are generally presented through text, stats, and management outcomes rather than cinematic gore, but descriptions can still be unsettling.

The game can also involve substance-related themes, including drug testing, failed tests, disciplinary consequences, rehab, and overdose-related deaths. Character relationships may include dating, marriage, breakups, and backstage conflict. Promotions can book more risqué creative product, and characters have adult attributes such as sexuality, but the core game is not built around explicit sexual content or depictions of sexual assault or non-consensual sex. Self-harm is not a featured theme of the base simulation.

Because the game supports custom mods and Steam Workshop content, user-created text, images, and scenarios may include stronger language or more sensitive topics than the base game. Players who want to avoid specific themes should review mods carefully before installing them.
